correctness.rationale: The ordinary-cut complement predicate gives exactly the dual's forbidden disconnected four-sets on the full nine-vertex ground set. In particular the full two-skeleton kills the fundamental group. Independent reconstruction of the finite certificate gives 81 connected and 45 disconnected four-sets, dual counts by size (1,9,36,84,81,36,6), and 69 legal collapses to (1,9,36,51,18). Exact unimodular reductions of d1,d2,d3 have 8,28,17 unit factors respectively and zero residual blocks. The collapsed two-skeleton is simply connected (attaching 3-cells does not affect pi1) and is equivalent to a wedge of 23 two-spheres by Hurewicz and homological Whitehead. The entire attaching map is a map from a wedge of 18 two-spheres into that wedge; it is classified by its integer degree matrix. The image of d3 is primitive in C2 and hence in ker(d2). Unimodular basis changes on either sphere wedge are realized by homotopy equivalences, so the attaching map can be put in the form identity on 17 summands and zero on the remaining attaching sphere. Its cofiber is six 2-spheres wedged with one 3-sphere. Alexander duality with degree 6-i and integral UCT then gives ranks 1 and 6 on the cut side in degrees 3 and 4; purity in dimension 4 and lower nonzero homology rule out shellability and Cohen–Macaulayness over any field.
residual_risks: The direct cut-side rank cross-check (8,28,50,39) is mod two; the cut-side integral assertion comes from duality. No homotopy type of the ordinary cut complex itself is concluded.

value.rationale: The first square rook board beyond clique-prism width isolates a natural threshold-four test. The integral mixed wedge is stronger than a face census or a Betti computation and gives a concrete nonshellable ordinary cut complex with next-to-top homology. It also supplies a base benchmark for the three-row extension.
residual_risks: Finite case only; no broader rook theorem, equivariant result or cut-side homotopy decomposition follows from the certificate.
